Hardware Firewall: Choosing the Right Firewall Distribution

The answer is pfSense or OPNSense. You can build or buy dedicated appliances for it, or you can build it on a KVM/ESX/whatever virtual host and set up a lot of bus-based vlans. Configure Snort, plop a PIA OpenVPN client config on a dedicated vlan for torr... er... guest traffic, set up traffic shaping, etc. There's plugins for syslog, nagios, and all kinds of local management stuff.

Other distributions like Untangle offer this kind of functionality, but at a price. I've heard of people running Untangle behind pfSense, and I even tried it for a while, but I never could identify any benefit to this beyond spinning cycles.
